key_facts: **Lipomas** are benign tumours of mature fat cells: soft, rubbery, mobile, painless lumps.
Commonest soft-tissue tumour; trunk, neck, shoulders and proximal limbs; usually under 5 cm.
Ultrasound if uncertain. **Sarcoma** features: over 5 cm, deep to fascia, growing, painful or recurrent: urgent imaging or referral (NICE suspected cancer).
Reassure; cosmetic removal is usually not NHS-funded.
Multiple painful lipomas: angiolipomas or **Dercum's disease**; multiple lipomas can be familial.

ul: **Lipoma:** a benign tumour of mature fat. The commonest soft-tissue tumour; age 40–60.
**Angiolipoma**: a vascular variant. Small (<2 cm), often **multiple and tender**, on the forearms and trunk of young adults (often men). Familial in about 5%.

**Dercum's disease (adiposis dolorosa)**: a rare chronic condition with **multiple painful lipomas or painful fatty tissue**, usually in obese women aged 35–50. It is often accompanied by fatigue, depression, sleep and cognitive problems, and joint pain. It is a diagnosis of exclusion.

Related syndromes: familial multiple lipomatosis; Madelung disease (benign symmetric lipomatosis, linked to alcohol); PTEN hamartoma (see *Other lumps and syndromes*); Gardner (see *Epidermoid, pilar and dermoid cysts; milia; Gardner syndrome*).

sub: Adults 40–60; about 1 in 100 people; more with obesity.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Lipomas show clonal rearrangements (often HMGA2 at 12q13–15). The cause of Dercum's pain is unclear; proposed mechanisms include nerve compression, inflammatory and neuroendocrine factors.

ul: Unknown; chromosomal rearrangements (12q13–15, HMGA2) in many; familial multiple lipomatosis; trauma possibly.
**"Lipomas turn into cancer"**: they almost never do; the concern is a sarcoma mistaken for a lipoma.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: A lipoma is a **capsule of normal-looking fat cells** growing slowly beneath the skin.

mech.t: Mature adipocytes proliferate as a lobulated mass with a thin fibrous capsule.
Growth is slow and then plateaus; the capsule makes it mobile and well defined.
Angiolipoma (vessels, tender), spindle-cell lipoma (back of neck in older men), deep lipomas within muscle.

histo: Mature adipocytes with a thin capsule; angiolipomas contain small vessels with microthrombi. Atypical lipomatous tumour shows atypical stromal cells (MDM2 amplification).

ul: Soft, rubbery, mobile, lobulated subcutaneous mass with normal overlying skin. Trunk, shoulders, neck and arms. Painless (except angiolipoma or Dercum).

**Red flags for sarcoma (refer):** size **>5 cm**, **increasing in size**, **deep to fascia** (fixed, doesn't move with the skin), **painful**, recurrence after excision. Thigh, buttock and retroperitoneal sites are higher risk, as is any lump that is hard or irregular.

fig.caption: Soft, mobile subcutaneous lipoma on the shoulder.

sub: Size over 5 cm, growth, pain, deep location, recurrence after excision: urgent ultrasound or sarcoma pathway.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Clinical for small, typical superficial lesions. **Ultrasound** is first-line imaging. MRI for deep or large lesions. Biopsy in a sarcoma centre, never by excision in primary care for a suspicious lump (an "unplanned excision" (the "whoops" procedure) compromises sarcoma outcomes).

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: Epidermoid cyst (punctum), liposarcoma and other soft-tissue sarcoma, lymph node, hernia, haematoma, neurofibroma (buttonhole sign), angiolipoma, lipodystrophy injection-site lipohypertrophy (insulin sites, so check injection technique).

ul: **Typical small lipoma:** reassure; removal for cosmetic reasons is usually not NHS-funded.

**NICE NG12 (sarcoma):** consider an **urgent direct-access ultrasound (performed within 2 weeks) for adults with an unexplained lump that is increasing in size**. Refer on the suspected cancer pathway if the ultrasound suggests sarcoma or is uncertain but clinical concern persists. In children/young people, an unexplained lump increasing in size warrants a **very urgent ultrasound (within 48 hours)**.
If the IP does not have direct-access imaging rights, the route is via the GP the same week, with the red flags documented.

**Dercum's disease:** a GP/specialist (dermatology, pain clinic) diagnosis. Management is symptomatic: analgesia, weight management, psychological support; specialist options include lidocaine infusions, liposuction and excision of the worst lesions. Screen for and support **depression**. Chronic pain medicines need careful IP review: avoid escalating opioids, and consider neuropathic agents per NICE NG193 (chronic primary pain) principles and local formulary.
**Lipohypertrophy from insulin/GLP-1 injections:** counsel on rotating sites. It also impairs absorption and glycaemic control.

refer.t: Lump that is increasing in size or larger than 5 cm, deep or painful: **urgent direct-access ultrasound** (within 2 weeks) or a suspected sarcoma pathway (NICE NG12).

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Lump that is increasing in size or larger than 5 cm, deep or painful: **urgent direct-access ultrasound** (within 2 weeks) or a suspected sarcoma pathway (NICE NG12).
Pressure on nerves; cosmetic concern; recurrence after excision (rare).

pearls: "Is it bigger than a golf ball, growing, deep or painful?" Then it needs a scan.
Angiolipoma tenderness is common and benign, but multiple painful lumps plus systemic symptoms should prompt thinking of Dercum.

quiz.q: When should you think of Lipoma & the sarcoma lump pathway?
quiz.a: A soft, painless, mobile, slowly growing lump on the trunk, neck or limbs.
Benign overgrowth of mature fat cells; angiolipomas are tender; Dercum’s disease gives many painful lipomas.

quiz.q: What is the backbone of care?
quiz.a: Reassure if small and typical; ultrasound or refer if uncertain; excision only for symptoms or diagnosis.
Soft-tissue sarcoma: larger than 5 cm, deep to fascia, growing, painful or recurrent.

quiz.a: Lump that is increasing in size or larger than 5 cm, deep or painful: **urgent direct-access ultrasound** (within 2 weeks) or a suspected sarcoma pathway (NICE NG12).
